agencies.name: Department of Forestry
agencies.role: Tracks fire hotspots through the Forestry Information Management System and reports them by forest category.

agencies.name: Department of Environment, Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry
agencies.role: Reported provincial PM2.5 readings against the national standard during the 2026 burning season.

monitoring.text: The Department of Forestry reported 16,395 hotspots between 1 January and 31 March 2026, and 895 on 1 April alone, according to the Lao News Agency.
The Lao News Agency reported that PM2.5 exceeded safety standards in nearly all provinces on 1 April 2026. No concentrations were given.

On 20 April 2026 the Department of Environment reported 24-hour PM2.5 of 239 µg/m³ in Pak Lay, 173 in Luang Prabang and 40 to 44 in Vientiane, against a national standard of 50 µg/m³, according to KPL.

seasonalPattern.text: ASMC's alerts for the northern ASEAN and Mekong region typically run from about December to May.

healthContext.text: Public health officials urged people to wear N95 or similar masks outdoors, avoid outdoor exercise and stop open burning.

dataAccess.name: Lao Agriculture News (Facebook page)
dataAccess.note: Named by KPL as the channel for daily official updates. No station data portal, download or API has been found.

openQuestions: Laos has a national 24-hour PM2.5 standard of 50 µg/m³, but whether it publishes a banded index, and how many stations it runs, has not been established.
No public PM2.5 data source has been found.
